title: He Is Fifteen. He Won the Orange Cap. Now He Is in India's Asian Games Squad.
excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest IPL Orange Cap winner with 776 runs at a strike rate of 237. The BCCI has picked him for the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya alongside Bumrah, Iyer, and Samson.
body:
The number is difficult to process. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is fifteen years old. In IPL 2026, playing for the Rajasthan Royals, he scored 776 runs in 16 innings at a strike rate of 237.30. He smashed 72 sixes. He won the Orange Cap, the tournament's award for the highest run-scorer, becoming the youngest player in IPL history to do so.

On Saturday, the BCCI went further. The teenager was named in India's 15-member squad for the 2026 Asian Games, to be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, this September. He will walk into a dressing room that includes Jasprit Bumrah, Sanju Samson, and Axar Patel. His captain will be Shreyas Iyer. He will represent India at a multi-sport event, in a full-strength squad, before he is old enough to drive.

## A Squad Built to Defend Gold

India won cricket gold at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where the sport returned to the programme for the first time since 2014. They are the defending champions, and unlike previous editions where the BCCI fielded development squads, this time the selectors have gone with firepower.

The full squad: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Tilak Varma (vice-captain), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, and Jasprit Bumrah.

The notable absentees are telling. Suryakumar Yadav, the former T20I captain, has been left out. So has Shubman Gill, who is leading the Test side against Afghanistan. Hardik Pandya, nursing a back injury from the latter stages of IPL 2026, has been excluded. Kuldeep Yadav is also missing, ruling him out of all of India's upcoming overseas assignments.

## The Bumrah Factor

The most significant inclusion beyond Sooryavanshi is Jasprit Bumrah. The fast bowler was rested from the ongoing Afghanistan series and from the upcoming T20I tours of Ireland and England to manage his workload after a gruelling first half of 2026. But the selectors have earmarked the Asian Games as his return assignment — a signal of how seriously the BCCI is treating the tournament.

The competition in Nagoya will run from September 24 to October 3 in the T20 format, overlapping with India's home series against the West Indies. That scheduling clash forced the BCCI to plan for two separate squads running simultaneously — the Asian Games team in Japan and a different group at home.

## Sooryavanshi's Meteoric Rise

Sooryavanshi's story has become one of Indian cricket's most compelling narratives. Born in 2011, he was barely a teenager when Rajasthan Royals picked him up at the IPL mega auction. His IPL debut came at 14, making him the youngest player to feature in the tournament. But it was the 2026 season that turned curiosity into conviction.

His 776 runs came against the best bowling attacks in the world — attacks featuring international stars who are more than twice his age. His strike rate of 237.30 was not a product of slogging; analysts noted his ability to pick lengths early, manufacture power through timing rather than brute force, and maintain composure in high-pressure chases. The 72 sixes included shots to all parts of the ground.

The call-up to the Asian Games squad came on the same day Sooryavanshi was named in India's T20I squad for the tours of Ireland and England. For the teenager, June 6 was the day two separate selection committees decided, independently, that he belonged at the highest level.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

The Asian Games hold a particular significance for the Indian diaspora in Japan. Aichi-Nagoya has a small but growing Indian community, largely connected to the automotive and tech industries. Cricket's inclusion in the programme gives that community a rare chance to watch India play live in their adopted home.

For the broader NRI audience, Sooryavanshi represents something generational — the proof that Indian cricket's talent pipeline, supercharged by the IPL's financial and competitive ecosystem, can produce players who are not just prodigies but competitors ready for the international stage before they finish school.

The Asian Games cricket competition begins on September 24. India's first match is yet to be announced. But when it comes, the youngest member of the squad will walk out knowing he has already done something no fifteen-year-old has done before.

*India's Asian Games squad: Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma (vc), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Ishan Kishan (wk), Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Jasprit Bumrah.*
